# RedwoodSDK: Rerunnable In-Memory REST Users API

## Background
A RedwoodSDK project is pre-installed at `/home/user/myapp`. Build a small JSON REST CRUD surface for users persisted in memory inside the worker module. All routes return JSON.

## Requirements
Implement the following endpoints under `/api/users`. Persist state in a module-level `Map<string, User>` (where `User` is `{ id: string; name: string; email: string }`). Generate IDs server-side (e.g. `crypto.randomUUID()`).

All endpoints must handle JSON payloads and return JSON responses with `Content-Type: application/json`.

- **GET `/api/users`**: Returns a status code of `200` with the body `{"users": [...]}` containing an array of all users sorted by insertion order. If there are no users, return an empty array.
- **POST `/api/users`**: Accepts a JSON body containing `{name, email}`. Returns a status code of `201` with the created user object `{id, name, email}` containing the newly generated ID.
  - If `name` or `email` is missing, or is not a string, return a status code of `400` with the body `{"error": "invalid payload"}`.
- **GET `/api/users/:id`**: Returns a status code of `200` with the user object if the user is found. If the user does not exist, return a status code of `404` with the body `{"error": "not found"}`.
- **PUT `/api/users/:id`**: Accepts a JSON body containing optional `{name?, email?}` fields. Updates the corresponding user and returns a status code of `200` with the updated user object. If the user does not exist, return a status code of `404`.
- **DELETE `/api/users/:id`**: Deletes the user with the given ID. Returns a status code of `204` with an empty body if the user is found and successfully deleted. If the user does not exist, return a status code of `404` with the body `{"error": "not found"}`.

# RedwoodSDK Minimal Starter

This is the starter project for RedwoodSDK. It's a template designed to get you up and running as quickly as possible.

Create your new project:

```shell
npx create-rwsdk my-project-name
cd my-project-name
npm install
```

## Running the dev server

```shell
npm run dev
```

Point your browser to the URL displayed in the terminal (e.g. `http://localhost:5173/`). You should see the RedwoodSDK welcome page in your browser.

## Further Reading

- [RedwoodSDK Documentation](https://docs.rwsdk.com/)
- [Cloudflare Workers Documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers)

The implementation is complete and verified. Here's a summary of what was built:

## Summary

I implemented an in-memory JSON REST Users API for the RedwoodSDK project at `/home/user/myapp`. The API is mounted in the worker module so state persists across requests.

### Files created/modified

**New file: `src/usersStore.ts`** — Holds the module-level `Map<string, User>` plus small helpers (`listUsers`, `getUser`, `createUser`, `updateUser`, `deleteUser`, `isValidUserPayload`). IDs are generated server-side via `crypto.randomUUID()`. `Map` insertion order is preserved by `Array.from(users.values())`.

**Modified: `src/worker.tsx`** — Added two method-based routes via `route()`:

- `route("/api/users", { get, post })`
- `route("/api/users/:id", { get, put, delete })`

Each handler returns `Response` objects with `Content-Type: application/json`. The router's method-based routing is used so each HTTP verb is dispatched correctly and unknown methods get a proper `405`.

### Verified behavior (live curl against `npm run dev`)

| Endpoint | Verified |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/users` empty → `200 {"users":[]}` | ✅ |
| `POST /api/users` valid → `201` with `{id,name,email}` | ✅ |
| `GET /api/users` populated → `200 {"users":[...insertion order]}` | ✅ |
| `GET /api/users/:id` found → `200` user | ✅ |
| `GET /api/users/:id` missing → `404 {"error":"not found"}` | ✅ |
| `PUT /api/users/:id` valid (name only, both) → `200` updated | ✅ |
| `PUT /api/users/:id` missing → `404 {"error":"not found"}` | ✅ |
| `DELETE /api/users/:id` exists → `204` empty | ✅ |
| `DELETE /api/users/:id` missing → `404 {"error":"not found"}` | ✅ |
| `POST /api/users` missing/non-string `name` or `email`, empty body → `400 {"error":"invalid payload"}` | ✅ |

`npx tsc --noEmit` passes with no errors.

Implemented and verified the in-memory REST Users API in the RedwoodSDK project at `/home/user/myapp`.

**Files:**
- `src/usersStore.ts` (new) — module-level `Map<string, User>` plus CRUD helpers; IDs generated with `crypto.randomUUID()`; insertion order preserved.
- `src/worker.tsx` (modified) — added `route("/api/users", { get, post })` and `route("/api/users/:id", { get, put, delete })` to the `defineApp([...])` chain.

**Behavior verified against the running dev server:**
- `GET /api/users` → 200 with `{"users":[...]}` (insertion-ordered; empty array when none)
- `POST /api/users` → 201 with `{id,name,email}`; 400 `{"error":"invalid payload"}` when `name`/`email` missing or not a string
- `GET /api/users/:id` → 200 with user; 404 `{"error":"not found"}` when missing
- `PUT /api/users/:id` → 200 with updated user; 404 `{"error":"not found"}` when missing
- `DELETE /api/users/:id` → 204 empty on success; 404 `{"error":"not found"}` when missing

All responses use `Content-Type: application/json`. `npx tsc --noEmit` passes cleanly.
